meta.title: In Spring — Set 1
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Comprehension quiz for 'In Spring' — understanding the author's opinion and main arguments.

questions.question: Why does the author think spring is the best season?
options: Because there are so many reasons to like it.
Because we can eat ice cream.
questions.explanation: The author asks, 'Why is spring the best season? There are so many reasons. Just ask me!'

questions.question: In spring, the days get warmer and longer.
questions.explanation: True. The text tells us: 'In spring, days get warmer' and 'In spring, days get longer.'

questions.question: What can you do after dinner in spring without a coat?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'You can run outside after dinner without a coat' because the days are longer and warmer.

questions.question: In spring, plants stop growing and trees lose all their leaves.
questions.explanation: False. In spring, 'plants start growing again' after the cold winter.

questions.question: Where can you walk in spring to spy flowers hiding?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'You can walk in the woods and spy flowers hiding behind trees.'

questions.question: In spring, you can see _______ coil up from underneath the wet ground.
questions.hint: Long, thin, legless animals that live in soil.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'You can see worms coil up from underneath the wet ground.'

questions.question: What can you wear to splash through puddles in spring?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'You can wear boots and splash through puddles' when the ground is wet.

questions.question: Sort these spring animals based on where they are seen in the story:
questions.explanation: Squirrels dart around, fawns walk in the woods/land, and worms coil up from the ground. Tadpoles swim in the pond's melting ice.

questions.question: You can see fawns struggling to walk on their young legs in spring.
questions.explanation: True. The text says: 'You can see fawns struggling to walk on their young legs.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to state the author's main opinion:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Spring is the best season.' This is what the author wants us to think.

questions.question: What does spring link together?
options: the cold of winter with the heat of summer
questions.explanation: The text says: 'It links the cold of winter with the heat of summer.'

questions.question: Spring waves _______ to winter and welcomes summer.
questions.hint: What you say when you leave.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'It waves good-bye to one season and welcomes another.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe the breezes of spring:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'You can feel breezes blow hints of hotter days.'

questions.question: In spring, you can see tadpoles swimming underneath the pond's melting ice.
questions.explanation: True. The text says: 'You can see tadpoles swimming beneath the pond's melting ice.'

questions.question: How does spring act as a connection between seasons?
options: It makes all seasons very dry.
It waves good-bye to winter and welcomes summer.
It stops plants from growing so winter stays.
It brings icicles to the hot summer.
questions.explanation: Spring links the seasons because it comes right after winter (waves good-bye to the cold) and right before summer (welcomes the heat).
